messages:
samir-support: FYI — Acme infra team hit a blocker on private/VPC deploy: model pulls + pip installs fail behind their firewall. They asked for a minimal egress allowlist for our devstack (model registry, auth, telemetry). Can we collect the canonical FQDNs and any OCSP/CRL endpoints?

maria-eng: sure. quick Q: are they doing TLS interception (corporate MITM) or strict SNI passthrough? that changes the OCSP/CRL bits. :thinking:

samir-support: customer says TLS is intercepted (Zscaler-like). errors in their logs: 403 from model-registry and "TLS: certificate verify failed" for pip. added a curl snippet below they sent: 

```
$ curl -v https://model-registry.acme.redwood-inference.internal/models/bert-shard-000 -o /dev/null
* About to connect() to model-registry.acme.redwood-inference.internal port 443
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* SSL: certificate verification failed (result: 5), subjectAltName does not match
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< Content-Type: application/json
< Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2025 13:22:01 GMT
< Content-Length: 145
{ ... }
```

raj-ops: thanks. two immediate things: 1) 403 indicates the request reached the registry but auth header may be stripped by MITM or proxy; 2) cert errors come from interception replacing certs. For allowlist we should ask them to allow passthrough for specific hosts and OCSP endpoints (or install our CA if they insist on interception).

maria-eng: minimal host list I usually give (canonical hosts we rely on):
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- models-cdn.redwood.ai (CDN for large shards)
- auth.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- files.pythonhosted.org
- pypi.org
- s3.amazonaws.com (for some model artifacts)
- packages.redwood.ai (internal package store)

Also OCSP/CRL and PKI checks:
- ocsp.digicert.com
- ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org
- crl.globalsign.net
- ocsp.pki.goog (if GCP is in path)

Ports: 443 outbound TCP (and allow large MTU/keepalive). If MITM is used, they need to preserve Authorization header and allow CONNECT/SNI passthrough for these FQDNs.

ops-jen: +1. note: telemetry uses CDN edges (Fastly/Cloudfront). customers that only allow IP CIDRs ask for ranges — we can provide AWS S3 IP ranges or Fastly backbone ranges on request but hostname allowlist is preferred for stability.

samir-support: can we provide a condensed checklist I can share with the customer (FQDNs + sample curl tests + what to ask their networking team)? Want this ASAP.

maria-eng: I'll draft a compact checklist. quick test commands to validate from their VPC: 
```
# check TLS and SNI passthrough
curl -vI https://model-registry.redwood.ai --resolve model-registry.redwood.ai:443:<their-egress-ip>

# test pip download (should return 200)
python -m pip download "requests==2.31.0" --dest /tmp/piptest

# test model shard (small sample)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://models-cdn.redwood.ai/sample-shard -o /tmp/shard
```
Include errors (headers + TLS debug) when escalating.

raj-ops: action items:
- maria-eng: publish one-pager checklist and list of FQDNs + OCSP hosts (owner)
- ops-jen: prepare note on IP ranges if customer needs CIDR (owner)
- samir-support: ask customer to run the three tests and paste outputs here (owner)

ops-jen: Also flag that customers behind TLS MITM often must whitelist our auth endpoint specifically to avoid Authorization header stripping. If they can't, suggest a temporary SSH bastion or egress proxy that doesn't MITM Redwood hosts.

support-bot: Reminder set (48h) for follow-up on thread 1789456123.

samir-support: shared checklist and tests with Acme; they ran curl + pip tests and attached logs — they still see SubjectAltName mismatch. Next step is to ask their SOC to either: 1) enable SNI passthrough for the above FQDNs, or 2) install their interception CA into the runtime truststore (we prefer passthrough).

maria-eng: if they install a CA, we need a note: runtime containers may use system cert store or Python cert bundles. they should install CA into both. we can provide exact paths for our installer if they want. :white_check_mark:

samir-support: thanks team — I'll keep this open and paste their logs in here when available. tagging @raj for any additional infra notes.

raj-ops: happy to help. once they confirm passthrough + allowed hosts, re-run tests. if still blocked we can request packet capture (redacted) or temporary access to their egress logs.

ops-jen: closing loop: when customer confirms allowlist we should document the edge case in KB: "Interception-causes-pip-and-model-pull-failures" and link to one-pager.

samir-support: noted, moving to follow-up state.
